result:
There is a particular hour, between four and five in the morning, when the world holds its breath. Not quite dark anymore, but not quite light. The stars have thinned to a handful of stubborn points, and the sky above is doing something slow and chemical, turning from black to the deep blue of a bruise healing.

I have stood on a balcony in that hour and felt the silence so completely that it had texture. It pressed against my eardrums like deep water. The radiator ticked. Somewhere three floors down, a dog coughed and stopped, as if embarrassed. A car passed on the distant highway, its headlights sweeping the underside of clouds, softening them into smudged cotton.

What strikes me is that this hour belongs to no one. It is not the morning of productivity, of coffee and the first email. It is not the night of dreaming. It is the seam between the two, the place where the world is neither one thing nor the other, and in that in-between, everything feels provisional. The buildings look like sketches. The trees are suggestions of trees.

I think about how we spend our lives mostly in the fully-lit middle or the fully-dark end, and rarely in this blue nothing. And yet the seam is where the real work happens. The world is not yet decided. It could go either way. And for one quiet minute, I like standing at the edge of a world that hasn't chosen its face for the day.
